documents.title: Integrate AI into your Teaching
documents.summary: CITL's campus teaching guidance frames generative AI as a transformative force faculty should engage with, listing faculty uses (drafting syllabi, rubrics, quiz items) and student learning uses (tutoring, study aids, brainstorming, writing support). It asks instructors to set clear course boundaries rather than a blanket syllabus ban, require citation of AI-generated content, attend to accuracy, privacy/FERPA, access and IP, and redesign assignments toward presentations, visible and multimodal work. It sets no campus-wide rule for students.

new_types.definition: Course staff state that they will not actively monitor or police students' AI use on the work in question, leaving the consequences to AI-free assessments or the student's own learning. Distinct from P39, which concerns the unreliability or non-use of AI detectors as evidence while enforcement continues by other means.

new_types.name: Instructor use of AI for teaching work
new_types.definition: What instructors or course staff may, should, or should not use AI for in their own teaching work: drafting syllabi, assignments, rubrics, quiz items, example datasets, course logistics (e.g., format conversion of schedules), translating or writing documents such as recommendation letters, and replying to student emails. Excludes grading (P46), disclosure of instructor AI use to students (P47), review and disclosure of AI-made course materials (P48), and research work such as manuscript peer review (outside teaching and learning).

notes: Reconciled consensus of two independent coders (v2 dry run). Collection notes: University layer: UIUC has no single campus AI policy; CITL's 'Integrate AI into your Teaching' is the campus teaching-center guidance. The University of Illinois System's 'Generative AI Guidance for Instructors' (https://www.vpaa.uillinois.edu/digital_risk_management/generative_ai/instructors), linked from CITL and Grainger, is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge (HTTP 403) and is INACCESSIBLE; it is system-level, not campus-level. Student Code Article 1 Part 4 (1-402) has no AI-specific text. genai.illinois.edu is a CIO tools/resources hub (excluded). genai.grainger.illinois.edu returns an intermittent IIS server error to fetch_text's user agent; both Grainger files were re-fetched until the full page saved. The Grainger guidance page embeds template tiers plus example course statements (BIOE 415 referenced, CS 411, NIU). Computing layer: no unit-level policy found for the Siebel School of Computing and Data Science, ECE, or the iSchool. Course layer: CS 124 has two documents (dedicated AI page and Fall 2026 syllabus) counted as one course. Also checked: CS 225 syllabus page (https://courses.grainger.illinois.edu/cs225/fa2026/policy/syllabus/, one-line AI rule, saved as v2-uiuc-cs225-syl but not listed), CS 173 (landing page only), CS 233 (PrairieLearn login), ECE 120 (HTTP 500). No other public iSchool syllabi with AI policies found. Reconciliation details and the reason for each resolved disagreement are in v2/dryrun/agreement_uiuc.json.
